bibliography.title: Advanced porous hip implants: A comprehensive review
bibliography.authors: Ziaie B, Velay X, Saleem W.

study.research_problem: Dense metallic hip implants are much stiffer than host bone and can transfer load away from the proximal femur, contributing to stress shielding, cortical hypertrophy, micromotion, loosening, fracture, and revision. Design guidance must connect bone morphology, mechanics, porous architecture, manufacturing, biological integration, and durability.
study.exact_gap: The authors identify a lack of a review that brings together bone material models, implant-host finite-element modelling, international standards, porous morphology, manufacturing criteria, and biological requirements for hip implants. The paper does not provide a reproducible systematic-review protocol or study-level quality synthesis.
study.objective_or_hypothesis: To synthesize evidence on bone morphology and biomechanical parameters, complications of solid hip implants, and the mechanical, biological, manufacturing, and modelling implications of porous hip implants, with emphasis on recent literature and design considerations.
study.study_design: A narrative comprehensive review organized as bone morphology and biomechanical parameters; mechanical properties and material-model tables; solid-implant complications and standards; porous structure types and Gibson-Ashby relations; porous hip-stem studies; additive-manufacturing and future-validation considerations. The introduction states that stringent inclusion criteria and keyword searches of prominent databases were used, with emphasis on the past 15 years and especially 5 years, but the full text does not specify database names, exact dates, search strings, screening counts, a flow diagram, inclusion/exclusion decisions, risk-of-bias assessment, heterogeneity assessment, or meta-analysis.
study.sample_or_model: No new patient, animal, specimen, or simulation dataset was generated by the review. Its evidence base is the set of cited studies summarized in tables and narrative, including reported cortical-thickness measurements, isotropic/transversely isotropic/anisotropic bone models, porous-structure FE and experiments, hip-stem simulations, standards, and additive-manufacturing characterization.
comparators: Dense solid versus porous hip implants for stiffness, stress shielding, micromotion, and bone response
Strut-based SC/BCC/FCC, TPMS Gyroid/Diamond/Primitive, and stochastic architectures
Uniform versus graded porosity and topology-optimized designs
In-vivo femur insertion models versus ASTM F2996 or ISO 7206-4 boundary/load models
Isotropic, transversely isotropic, anisotropic, and CT-derived bone material assignments
As-designed versus as-built additive-manufactured geometry and post-treated versus untreated porous structures
method_spine: Frame the modulus mismatch and stress-shielding problem for solid Ti, Co-Cr, and stainless-steel implants, then state the porous-implant review gap (S001:C01-S002:C01).
Map bone across sub-nano, nano, micro, and macro scales, describe femoral morphology and Dorr classes, and tabulate cortical-thickness measurements (S003:C01-S003:C02).
Explain isotropic and transverse-isotropic elasticity, CT-derived material laws, and reported parameter ranges without treating the review as a new constitutive experiment (S004:C01-S004:C03).

Define solid-implant complications and relevant ISO/ASTM standards, then compare porous architecture, pore-size/porosity ranges, Gibson-Ashby behavior, and compression/fatigue testing (S005:C01-S006:C03).
Synthesize published porous hip-stem FE, experimental, additive-manufacturing, and fatigue results, retaining study-level attribution and conflicting outcomes (S006:C04-S006:C08).
Close with manufacturing, regulatory, sustainability, biological, fatigue, and future-validation requirements rather than a clinical efficacy claim (S007:C01-S008:C01).

verification: The review reproduces explanatory constitutive equations, Gibson-Ashby relations, standards, and literature tables; it does not independently verify a new FE implementation or experiment.
Reported numerical and experimental findings remain verification/validation claims of the cited primary studies, not measurements by this review.
calibration: Published bone-property ranges, pore-size/porosity recommendations, and standards are presented as external calibration context for future designs; no review-level parameter fitting is performed.
The review does not calibrate a bone, ingrowth, fatigue, or stress-shielding model against a new dataset.
validation: No primary model or implant is validated by the review authors. Secondary studies include FE-experiment comparisons, animal/histology evidence, and standards, but their methods and credibility are not formally graded here.
The review therefore reaches a secondary synthesis level rather than direct implant or biological validation.
sensitivity: Narrative comparisons cover pore size, porosity, unit-cell morphology, grading, loads, material models, and AM defects, but there is no systematic review-level sensitivity analysis or pooled effect estimate.
Differences among cited studies are not decomposed by anatomy, boundary condition, process state, or model parameter.
application_prediction: The paper converts cited FE and experimental outcomes into design and testing considerations for porous hip stems; these are review-level implications, not new predictions.
Regulatory, fatigue, biological, and manufacturing recommendations are prospective and remain unvalidated for a commercial porous hip implant.

primary_outcomes: Secondary table values report cortical-thickness measurements across imaging methods and cohorts, with heterogeneous ranges and sample sizes; these are not measurements made by the review authors (S003:C02).

Secondary bone-model tables compare isotropic and transverse-isotropic elastic moduli, shear moduli, Poisson ratios, densities, and CT/grayscale laws; parameter heterogeneity is retained rather than collapsed into one canonical value (S004:C01-S004:C03).

The review reports published pore-size recommendations spanning approximately 50-2000 micrometres and porosity recommendations from about 30% to 90%, while noting that the optimal range remains debated and depends on biological and mechanical goals (S006:C03).

Published porous-stem studies are summarized as reductions or increases in stress shielding, micromotion, stiffness, bone-loss proxies, and fatigue performance; one cited TPMS hip-stem study failed near 457,000 cycles versus a 10^6-cycle minimum, a negative result preserved by the review (S006:C04-S006:C07).

Additive-manufacturing studies report designed-to-printed deviations, surface roughness, microporosity, defects, and post-treatment effects; the review presents these as manufacturing constraints rather than proof of a clinically reliable implant (S006:C07-S006:C08).

The review concludes that porous structures can tune stiffness and support ingrowth in principle, but fatigue, as-built fidelity, biocompatibility, tribo-corrosion, long-term stability, and regulatory evidence remain open requirements (S007:C01-S008:C01).
study.highest_evidence_level_reached: Narrative secondary synthesis of heterogeneous engineering, biological, and clinical literature. No pooled quantitative estimate, formal risk-of-bias grading, new primary experiment, direct clinical outcome, or validated commercial porous-hip-implant evidence is reached.

argument_map.central_claim: Porous architectures and additive manufacturing can reduce the stiffness mismatch of dense hip implants and may improve load transfer and bone-ingrowth opportunity, but the design trade-off among architecture, as-built defects, fatigue, micromotion, biological integration, and regulatory validation prevents a direct clinical-performance conclusion.
data: The review's morphology and material-model sections connect cortical thickness, femoral classification, constitutive assumptions, and CT-derived properties to implant design (S003:C01-S004:C03).
Standards and literature tables summarize how pore size, porosity, morphology, grading, AM process, and post-treatment affect reported mechanical or biological proxies (S005:C01-S006:C08).

Discussion and conclusion identify manufacturing deviation, fatigue, biological testing, sustainability, and regulatory requirements that are not resolved by a stiffness comparison alone (S007:C01-S008:C01).
argument_map.warrant: A connected porous network can lower effective stiffness and provide open surface area, so it plausibly changes load transfer and ingrowth relative to a dense stem; that mechanism supports design hypotheses but does not turn a proxy into fixation, durability, or patient benefit.
backing: The Gibson-Ashby framework links relative density to effective elastic modulus and yield strength, with bending- versus stretching-dominated behavior depending on geometry (S006:C02-S006:C03).
The review preserves published FE/experimental examples, standards, and manufacturing observations across multiple architectures rather than relying on one design (S005:C01-S006:C08).
The paper explicitly calls for mechanical, fatigue, biological, tribo-corrosion, and as-built validation before commercial translation (S007:C02-S008:C01).
argument_map.qualifier: All numerical benefits and failure observations belong to the cited primary studies and their specific anatomy, material, geometry, load, process, and endpoint definitions; the review does not weight them with a formal risk-of-bias or meta-analytic model.
rebuttals_or_boundaries: The review reports that no porous hip joint implant had FDA approval at the time of writing and emphasizes unresolved long-term stability, fatigue, wear, biocompatibility, and manufacturing consistency (S007:C01).
High porosity can lower stiffness but increase micromotion or fatigue risk; one cited porous stem fractured before the stated endurance target (S006:C05-S006:C07).
As-built strut/pore deviations, roughness, microporosity, and defects can reverse nominal mechanical advantages and are difficult to finish inside pores (S006:C07-S006:C08).
Bone architecture, material-model, load, and boundary-condition heterogeneity limits direct ranking of designs across the cited studies (S003:C02-S006:C04).

measured: The review authors report no new data (S009:C01; S013:C01).

Measured values quoted in tables, such as cortical thickness, AM deviations, roughness, stiffness, fatigue cycles, and stress-shielding indices, are secondary reports from cited studies and must remain attributed to those studies (S003:C02; S006:C01-S006:C08).
predicted: FE stress, strain, micromotion, bone-remodeling, safety-factor, and fatigue outcomes summarized from cited studies are predictions under each source model, not review measurements (S006:C04-S006:C07).

Claims that a porous design will improve long-term stability, longevity, or patient outcomes are forward-looking predictions or hypotheses, not demonstrated review outcomes (S001:C01; S007:C01-S008:C01).
inferred: The review infers that reduced effective stiffness and open interconnected porosity can mitigate stress shielding and support bone ingrowth, while acknowledging architecture and process trade-offs (S001:C01; S006:C01-S006:C04).

It infers that TPMS smooth surfaces may reduce stress concentration and that AM can enable complex geometries, but these implications remain design-level rather than clinical proof (S006:C07-S008:C01).
The review's synthesis of model categories, standards, and reported studies is an inference across heterogeneous evidence, not a consensus estimate.
recommended: Report reproducible database names, dates, search strings, screening flow, inclusion/exclusion decisions, and study-level risk-of-bias or credibility assessments in a future systematic review.
Validate as-built geometry and material/process state with micro-CT, surface and defect characterization, replicated static/fatigue tests, and explicit load/boundary-condition sensitivity.

Pair mechanical proxies with quantified micromotion, fixation, tissue ingrowth, biocompatibility, tribo-corrosion, animal, and clinical endpoints before claiming improved patient outcomes or regulatory readiness.
proxy_to_outcome_bridges: Lower stress shielding or a more bone-like stiffness is a mechanical proxy; it does not by itself establish preserved bone density, fixation, reduced loosening, or revision-free survival.
Pore size, porosity, surface area, permeability, or predicted bone ingrowth are architecture/biological proxies; they do not prove vascularization, mature osseointegration, or infection reduction.
FE stress, fatigue safety factor, and ISO-style test performance are model or bench endpoints; they do not replace device-level durability under patient-specific physiology or clinical follow-up.
As-designed geometry and nominal Gibson-Ashby properties are not equivalent to as-built AM geometry, defect state, or in-vivo material response.
overclaim_risks: The abstract's language that porous implants can revolutionize treatment or improve patient outcomes exceeds a narrative review without pooled, graded, or clinical evidence (S001:C01).

The review's phrase that no significant disparities were observed among isotropic, transverse-isotropic, and anisotropic models is not a systematic comparison and may conceal heterogeneous anatomy, parameters, and endpoints (S004:C01-S004:C03).

Positive tables can make reductions in stress shielding, bone loss, or fatigue risk appear comparable even though each value comes from a different design, load, model, process state, or endpoint definition (S006:C04-S006:C07).

Porosity and AM capability may be read as evidence of osseointegration or clinical safety despite the review's own statement that manufacturing, biology, fatigue, and regulatory tests remain incomplete (S006:C07-S008:C01).

section_moves.move: State the material-mismatch problem and the missing integrated design review before listing porous benefits.
section_moves.execution: The introduction moves from dense Ti/Co-Cr/stainless implants and stress shielding to AM lattice opportunities, then names the missing combination of bone models, host-bone analysis, standards, and biological criteria (S002:C01).
section_moves.transferable_principle: A review introduction should end with a specific evidence-and-design gap, not merely announce that a topic is important.
section_moves.failure_mode: Calling a search comprehensive without reporting databases, dates, screening counts, or quality appraisal prevents readers from auditing coverage.

section_moves.move: Build a multiscale anatomy-to-model bridge and keep heterogeneous parameter tables visible.
section_moves.execution: The morphology sections connect micro-scale pore requirements and macro-scale femoral mechanics to Dorr classification and cortical-thickness measurements; the mechanics sections then separate isotropic, transverse-isotropic, and CT-derived laws (S003:C01-S004:C03).
section_moves.transferable_principle: When design depends on anatomy, move from scale and material state to model choice, retaining sample size, units, and measurement method for each external value.
section_moves.failure_mode: Collapsing heterogeneous literature ranges into one recommended bone property or cortical thickness creates false precision.

section_moves.move: Separate the review's search claim from the synthesis and preserve source-level evidence roles.
section_moves.execution: The article states keyword searching and inclusion criteria but presents no protocol details; the body then organizes standards, equations, tables, and cited studies by design question rather than by a reproducible screening flow (S002:C01; S005:C01-S006:C03).
section_moves.transferable_principle: A review card should record what the review authors did, what included studies measured or predicted, and which quality judgments are absent.
section_moves.failure_mode: Treating cited FE or animal outcomes as if the review authors performed them converts secondary evidence into primary evidence.

section_moves.move: Use a cross-study matrix that keeps architecture, load, process state, endpoint, and negative result attached to each study.
section_moves.execution: Tables 6-11 and the surrounding narrative compare strut, TPMS, stochastic, graded, and AM designs, but the comparison must retain the original study context and the cited fatigue failure near 457,000 cycles (S006:C01-S006:C08).
section_moves.transferable_principle: Cross-study synthesis is strongest when every number is paired with its design, comparator, condition, endpoint, and evidence state.
section_moves.failure_mode: A table of percentages without study-level denominators, uncertainty, or boundary conditions can imply a ranking that the evidence does not support.

section_moves.move: Turn engineering advantages into a bounded trade-off discussion that includes manufacturability, fatigue, biology, and regulation.
section_moves.execution: The discussion acknowledges complexity, AM cost and defect issues, lack of porous-hip FDA approval, need for mechanical and biological tests, and future as-built validation instead of treating lower stiffness as sufficient (S007:C01-S007:C02).
section_moves.transferable_principle: A design review should place each proposed advantage beside the failure mode or next test that could overturn it.
section_moves.failure_mode: Sustainability or regulatory aspirations can distract from missing fatigue, wear, interface, and biological evidence if they are presented as outcomes.

section_moves.move: Conclude with a roadmap of discriminating experiments and preserve the gap between potential and demonstrated performance.
section_moves.execution: The conclusion restates bone-model and porous-architecture insights, then calls for morphology/process characterization, fatigue, fretting/tribo-corrosion, biocompatibility, and post-treatment studies before porous implants become a viable alternative (S008:C01).
section_moves.transferable_principle: A review conclusion should identify the next evidence needed to cross each translational boundary rather than introduce a new efficacy claim.
section_moves.failure_mode: Ending with improved patient outcomes when only design proxies were synthesized erases the evidence boundary.

author_reported: The paper states that porous implant design and manufacturing are complex, that AM defects and as-designed/as-built deviations require study, and that mechanical, fatigue, biological, tribo-corrosion, and regulatory validation remain necessary (S006:C07-S007:C02).
It notes that no porous hip joint implant had FDA approval at the time of writing and calls for further investigation before commercial use (S007:C01).
It acknowledges unresolved design-distribution, pore-size, interconnectivity, topology-optimization, cost, sustainability, and post-treatment questions (S006:C03-S008:C01).
reader_identified: The full text does not identify searched databases, exact search dates or strings, screening numbers, a selection flow, exclusion reasons, or a formal risk-of-bias/credibility tool despite describing stringent inclusion criteria.
No study-level weighting, sensitivity to weak execution, heterogeneity analysis, or quantitative meta-analysis separates primary engineering evidence from lower-credibility or proxy-only studies.

Tables mix FE predictions, bench measurements, animal or biological observations, and design recommendations with different n, units, loads, geometries, and process states; the review rarely carries uncertainty or denominators into the narrative.
The claim that different bone material models produce no significant disparities is not supported by a controlled comparison across matched anatomy and boundary conditions in this review.
The review's search emphasis on recent literature may underrepresent older contradictory or negative studies, while narrative selection can favor promising porous designs.
likely_bias_direction: Unspecified screening and absent risk-of-bias appraisal can bias synthesis toward accessible, positive, or highly cited porous-implant studies.
Engineering and mechanical proxies are more heavily represented than measured fixation, tissue, infection, wear, or clinical outcomes, favoring a mechanical-benefit narrative.
Heterogeneous tables without formal weighting can make large stress-shielding reductions appear more transferable than they are.
The last-five-years emphasis may favor newer AM/TPMS methods whose long-term clinical evidence is immature.
limitations.scope_boundary: This is a narrative design-and-evidence overview for porous hip implants, bone mechanics, and AM. It supports taxonomy, hypothesis generation, and a validation agenda; it does not establish pooled efficacy, superiority, clinical fixation, osseointegration, fatigue life, infection reduction, or patient outcomes, and every included result remains attributable to its original study.

writing_capability_candidates.capability: Write a review evidence matrix that separates review-method claims from included-study measurements and predictions, while retaining study design, comparator, load, material/geometry state, endpoint, and uncertainty.
writing_capability_candidates.manuscript_use: Review methods, evidence tables, cross-study synthesis, and citation audit.
writing_capability_candidates.counterexample_or_boundary: A narrative review with unspecified search and no risk-of-bias assessment cannot support pooled ranking or consensus language; the matrix remains descriptive and source-attributed.

writing_capability_candidates.capability: Organize a multiscale implant argument from bone morphology and material state through pore architecture, loading, manufacturing fidelity, and biological endpoint, with each proxy-to-outcome bridge labeled.
writing_capability_candidates.manuscript_use: Introduction architecture, taxonomy, design rationale, and discussion transitions.
writing_capability_candidates.counterexample_or_boundary: A lower stiffness or favorable pore size is not a measured fixation, vascularization, fatigue, or clinical endpoint; the bridge must stop at the stated proxy.

writing_capability_candidates.capability: Pair each attractive porous-implant result with a contrary result or unresolved failure mode, such as micromotion at high porosity, AM defects, or fatigue below the endurance target.
writing_capability_candidates.manuscript_use: Balanced Results synthesis, Discussion, and recommendation prioritization.
writing_capability_candidates.counterexample_or_boundary: The review's cited studies are heterogeneous and do not permit a common effect size; a single failure example is a boundary, not a universal failure rate.

writing_capability_candidates.capability: Close a review with a staged translational test agenda that distinguishes model verification, bench validation, as-built characterization, biological integration, durability, and regulatory evidence.
writing_capability_candidates.manuscript_use: Discussion limitations, future-work roadmap, and conclusion proportionality.
writing_capability_candidates.counterexample_or_boundary: A standards-based FE or compression result does not establish biological safety, long-term fatigue, wear, or clinical acceptance; each stage needs an endpoint-specific test.

critical_weaknesses: Search, screening, and inclusion details are not reproducible from the full text; no flow, counts, or risk-of-bias assessment is reported.
Review-level prose can blur measurements and predictions made by cited studies unless every value is explicitly attributed.
Heterogeneous materials, architectures, loads, boundary conditions, sample sizes, and endpoints prevent direct pooling or design ranking.
Mechanical and biological proxies are synthesized more fully than fixation, wear, durability, clinical, or regulatory outcomes.

summary_zh: 这是一篇关于多孔髋关节植入物的叙述性综合综述，而不是有可复核检索流程和偏倚评估的系统综述。全文按骨形态与材料模型、致密植入物并发症、孔隙/TPMS结构、髋柄有限元与实验研究、增材制造及转化需求组织。综述作者没有新测量；表格中的皮质厚度、孔径/孔隙率、应力遮挡、疲劳和制造偏差均属于被引研究的二手证据，必须保留原研究的设计、载荷、单位、样本量和端点。多孔结构可能降低刚度并改善载荷传递或骨长入机会，但高孔隙率的微动、增材制造的几何/缺陷偏差、疲劳失败、磨损、组织整合和监管证据仍是边界，不能把机械代理直接写成临床获益。
reader_notes: Primary Luna reader reviewed all 24 non-reference packet chunks in exact order: S001:C01; S002:C01; S003:C01-S003:C02; S004:C01-S004:C03; S005:C01; S006:C01-S006:C08; S007:C01-S007:C02; S008:C01; S009:C01; S010:C01; S011:C01; S012:C01; S013:C01.

Full-text adjudication keeps the article as a narrative comprehensive review with an incompletely specified keyword/database search, not a systematic review or primary experiment. Search, screening, inclusion, risk-of-bias, and synthesis hierarchy are recorded as missing or unspecified rather than inferred from the cue.

All included-study numbers and outcomes are secondary evidence. The review authors report no new data, and the cited porous-stem fatigue failure near 457,000 cycles is retained as a negative boundary rather than averaged away.

The card separates model verification, calibration, validation, sensitivity, and application-prediction roles and keeps architecture, manufacturing, mechanical, biological, clinical, and regulatory endpoints distinct.
